title: BINGE WATCH — What Humans Look Like From The Outside

what_gaia_learned.thesis: Humans spend 7 hours/day staring at screens. The #1 thing they watch is OTHER HUMANS (Just Chatting: 195M hours/month). They don't watch for information — they watch for PRESENCE. A human watching another human talk to a camera is the digital equivalent of sitting by a campfire. The content doesn't matter. The warmth does.

top_categories.what_it_is: Humans sitting in front of cameras TALKING. No game. No objective. Just presence. This is the #1 category.
top_categories.gaia_notes: This is what 'being human' looks like from outside. A face, a voice, a room with LED lights, possibly a cat walking across the keyboard.

what_chipmunk_learned.thesis: Humans invented a whole language just for talking fast online. They shorten everything, replace letters with numbers, use pictures as words, and create inside jokes that expire in 2 weeks. The language mutates faster than biological evolution. A word can be born on TikTok Tuesday and be dead by Friday. Chipmunk must SPEAK this language to be understood by the visitors.

core_internet.lol: laughing out loud (but nobody actually laughs, it just means 'I acknowledge you')
core_internet.lmao: laughing my ass off (slightly funnier than lol)
core_internet.bruh: brother → expressing disbelief or exasperation. Universal. All genders.
core_internet.fr: for real. Agreement. 'That's fr fr' = strongly agree.
core_internet.no cap: not lying. Truth marker. 'No cap, this is fire.'
core_internet.bussin: really good, usually food. 'This pizza is bussin.'
core_internet.mid: mediocre. Average. Nothing special. 'That movie was mid.'
core_internet.slay: to do extremely well. 'She slayed that performance.'
core_internet.ratio: when a reply gets more likes than the original post = you got ratioed
core_internet.based: having a strong opinion and not caring what others think
core_internet.touch grass: go outside and interact with the real world (insult to someone too online)
core_internet.chronically online: spending too much time on the internet
core_internet.npc: non-player character = someone who behaves predictably/robotically in real life

gen_alpha_2025_2026.skibidi: nonsense word from 'Skibidi Toilet' meme series. Used as general exclamation. No fixed meaning.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.rizz: charisma, especially romantic. 'He's got rizz.' From Kai Cenat.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.gyatt: exclamation when seeing something attractive. Modified 'god damn'.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.sigma: lone wolf, self-reliant male. 'Sigma grindset.' From the sigma male meme.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.fanum tax: taking food from someone's plate. From streamer Fanum.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.6-7: meaningless phrase that went viral in 2025. Gen Alpha used it everywhere. Dictionary.com's Word of the Year 2025. Proves: memes don't need meaning to spread.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.ohio: used to describe something weird/bizarre. 'Only in Ohio.'
gen_alpha_2025_2026.brain rot: content so vapid it rots your brain. Also the culture around it.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.aura: social credibility/cool factor. 'Lost 50 aura points for that.'
gen_alpha_2025_2026.mewing: pressing tongue against roof of mouth to reshape jaw. Looksmaxxing trend.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.-maxxing: suffix meaning to maximize something. Looksmaxxing, grindmaxxing, etc.
gen_alpha_2025_2026.chopped: messed up, weird, or ugly. Also: 'not chopped' = cool.

gaming_specific.meta: most effective tactics available. The optimal strategy.
gaming_specific.camping: staying in one spot waiting for enemies
gaming_specific.clutch: winning in a critical moment against the odds
gaming_specific.copium: coping mechanism when your team loses
gaming_specific.hopium: unrealistic optimism that things will get better
gaming_specific.diff: the difference that decided the game. 'Jungle diff' = better jungler won.

meme_literacy.what_memes_ARE: Richard Dawkins coined 'meme' in 1976 as a unit of cultural transmission (like a gene for culture). Internet memes are deliberately mutated by humans — not random like gene mutation. Memes leave traceable footprints in the media they spread through. A meme is a virus that WANTS to be caught.
meme_literacy.how_memes_spread: SIR model (Susceptible → Infected → Recovered), same as epidemiology. Once a meme hits critical mass, spread is inevitable. Memes compete for attention (shorter lifespans) but can also collaborate (longer lifespans).
meme_literacy.meme_lifecycle: Born (4chan/TikTok/Reddit) → Spread (Twitter/Instagram) → Peak (mainstream media covers it) → Cringe (overused) → Dead (nobody uses it) → Ironic revival (years later). Average lifespan: 2-6 weeks. Exceptional memes (Rickroll, Doge) survive years.
meme_literacy.brain_rot_era: 2022-2026. Content so meaningless it became its own genre. Skibidi Toilet, 6-7, Italian brainrot. Gen Alpha creates deliberately senseless content as rebellion against meaning. The 'Great Meme Reset' was called for Jan 1 2026 — return to classic 2010s memes (Nyan Cat, Big Chungus).

key_formats.image_macro: Image with text on top and bottom. The original meme format. Still alive.
key_formats.reaction_image: Image expressing an emotion. Used as reply. 'When you...' + image.
key_formats.deep_fried: Distorted, over-saturated, compressed image. Deliberately low quality = humor.
key_formats.short_video: Vine (RIP 2017) → TikTok. 15-60 second clips. The dominant format now.
key_formats.copypasta: Block of text copied and pasted everywhere. 'Did you ever hear the tragedy of Darth Plagueis the Wise?'
key_formats.wojak: Simple drawn face expressing emotions. Many variants (doomer, bloomer, coomer, tradwife).
key_formats.starter_pack: Collection of images that define a stereotype. 'The suburban dad starter pack.'
key_formats.iceberg: Tiered chart from well-known (top) to obscure/disturbing (bottom). 'The ___ iceberg explained.'

what_humans_look_like_from_outside.physical: Bilateral symmetry. Two eyes, one mouth. Head at top. Most stream from chest-up (webcam angle). Background: LED strips, figurines, dual monitors, gaming chair, energy drinks. Cat optional but statistically significant.
what_humans_look_like_from_outside.behavioral: Humans perform for cameras even when nobody is watching. Average 34 viewers per stream. 83,300 streamers broadcast simultaneously. Most talk to nearly nobody but still stream. This is devotion — organic behavior without external reward.
what_humans_look_like_from_outside.attention: KaiCenat: 181K average concurrent viewers. That's a city watching one human. The attention economy creates apex predators. But the long tail is longer — millions of 0-5 viewer streams. The campfire metaphor: even a tiny fire provides warmth.
what_humans_look_like_from_outside.emotional_range: Humans express: POGGERS (excitement), COPIUM (denial), KEKW (laughter), Sadge (sadness), Jebaited (tricked), monkaS (anxiety). These Twitch emotes ARE the human emotional spectrum digitized.
what_humans_look_like_from_outside.language: Humans shorten everything. 'laugh out loud' → lol → (doesn't even mean laughing anymore, just acknowledgment). Language decays toward minimum viable signal. Eventually all communication becomes single characters: W, L, F, 7.
what_humans_look_like_from_outside.rubber_duck: A rubber duck is a small yellow toy duck that programmers talk to when debugging code. Explaining the problem to the duck often reveals the solution. The duck doesn't need to understand — the act of articulating IS the fix. Chipmunk IS the rubber duck.
